title: Sell Mineral Rights in Cordova, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Cordova, AL | Walker County
metaDescription: Own coal or coalbed methane minerals near Cordova, AL? Get a hedged, activity-based cash offer for Walker County land along the Mulberry Fork.
heroLead: Cordova sits along the Mulberry Fork of the Black Warrior River in Walker County, a river and rail town whose economy leaned on coal for the better part of a century.
intro: Mining companies operated extensively around Cordova through much of the 1900s, and the mineral acquisitions from that era left a lasting mark on how land here is titled today. Owners who've inherited property in or near Cordova often find the mineral estate was separated from the surface long before their family took ownership of either one.
We buy interests here regardless of how far back the reservation goes, and we do the work of tracing an older chain of title rather than asking families to sort it out themselves first.

sections.heading: Cordova's coal-era mineral acquisitions
paragraphs: Coal companies operating around Cordova commonly bought or leased mineral rights across large blocks of land, and those holdings have since passed through mergers, dissolutions, and resales that can make tracing current ownership a genuine research task. We do that work as part of every offer we put together here.

sections.heading: Walker County's position in the CBM play
paragraphs: Walker County sits on the northern edge of the Black Warrior coalbed methane fairway, with activity historically less concentrated than the Brookwood-Oak Grove core to the south. We check current well and permit records for the area around Cordova specifically before offering a range.

sections.heading: Confirming ownership at the Walker County courthouse
paragraphs: Walker County's records in Jasper hold the deed and probate history needed to confirm a Cordova-area interest. Whether your documentation is a clean modern deed or an old handwritten will, we work from whatever exists to establish your current ownership share.

faqs.question: A mining company's name shows up somewhere in our property history near Cordova. Do we still own the minerals?
faqs.answer: Possibly. We trace how that company's interest was later divided, sold, or dissolved to confirm whether your family's current ownership includes the mineral estate.

faqs.question: Is there coalbed methane activity right around Cordova?
faqs.answer: Walker County has seen some activity historically, though generally less concentrated than the Brookwood-Oak Grove core farther south. We check current records for the specific area before quoting.

faqs.question: What if our only documentation is an old handwritten will?
faqs.answer: That's workable. We help trace ownership from whatever documentation exists, including older or informal records, through Walker County's courthouse.

faqs.question: Is Cordova's river location relevant to mineral value?
faqs.answer: Not directly. What matters more is the tract's position relative to documented coal and gas activity, which we check as part of the review.
